papers.title: Characterizing transition state in mouse vigilance with electroencephalogram-electromyogram hypnodensity.
papers.summary: This study characterized vigilance-state transitions in mice using EEG/EMG recordings and expert annotations, revealing distinct temporal dynamics (NREMS-to-REMS transitions longest, REMS-to-NREMS most abrupt) and validating SVM classifiers trained on stable-state features to predict transition midpoints despite moderate inter-rater variability.

papers.title: REM Sleep Disengagement of β Oscillations Permits Rapid Dream Movements in Parkinsonism
papers.summary: In non-human primates with MPTP-induced parkinsonism, REM sleep attenuated pathological beta oscillations and motor impairments that were prominent during wakefulness and NREM sleep, with beta suppression starting before REM onset, indicating brain-state-dependent gating of Parkinsonian network dysfunction and latent capacity for rapid movement.

papers.title: Diurnal time and sleep pressure modulate cerebrospinal fluid low-frequency oscillations in synchrony with wake-promoting nuclei
papers.summary: Using a 34-hour sleep deprivation study with fMRI/EEG/NIRS, the authors found that cerebrospinal fluid low-frequency oscillations (LFOs) increased with time awake and peaked in early morning, correlating with vigilance and reticular activating system activity but not plasma norepinephrine, demonstrating independent modulation by sleep pressure and diurnal time.

papers.title: Meta-Analysis of Face-Validity Indicators in Automatically Detected Dog Sleep Spindles.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis of face validity indicators for automatically detected dog sleep spindles applied three criteria (short duration, midline distribution of fast spindles, amplitude-negative chirp association) across datasets, finding majority compliance and supporting both the detection method and the dog as a model for human spindle research.

papers.title: Leednet: a lightweight network for event detection in EEG signals.
papers.summary: LEEDNet, a lightweight convolutional network for EEG event detection, achieved 81.2% accuracy and 77.5% macro-F1 on the NMT-Events dataset with only 0.25M parameters and <5ms inference, outperforming baselines; 2-second segments and raw EEG inputs were optimal, with no gains from FFT or wavelet features.

papers.title: Epi-Spec2State: Convolutional state space model via spectrogram image sequences for prediction-oriented seizure state classification in EEG signals.
papers.summary: This paper introduces Epi-Spec2State, a convolutional state space model that transforms EEG signals into spectrogram image sequences for seizure state classification. On a private SEEG dataset, it achieved 96.40-96.60% accuracy and 98.20-98.30% specificity, and outperformed nine state-of-the-art methods on public datasets in mixed-subject and cross-subject evaluations.

papers.title: Fully-automated sleep staging for Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: This study fine-tuned the U-Sleep deep neural network for automated sleep staging in Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, improving Cohen's kappa from 0.66 to 0.74 after fine-tuning and achieving human-level agreement. Confidence-based thresholds increased REM precision from 85% to 95.6% while preserving sufficient REM sleep in 96% of subjects.

papers.title: Respiratory phase shapes brain-heart dynamics: evidence from recurrence analysis of EEG band power and heart rate.
papers.summary: This study investigated respiratory-phase-dependent modulation of brain-heart interactions during controlled breathing using EEG band power and heart rate in 15 healthy subjects. Inhale-hold was associated with increased gamma band power, higher recurrence rate, and elevated heart rate, whereas exhale-hold showed reduced gamma activity, lower recurrence, and decreased heart rate, indicating distinct autonomic states.

papers.title: Aftereffects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia on the jaw muscle electromyographic activities during sleep in young adult rats.
papers.summary: This study examined the aftereffects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) on jaw muscle activity during sleep in young adult rats. CIH increased FosB expression in brainstem regions and noradrenergic fiber density in the trigeminal motor nucleus, and selectively increased digastric muscle activity during arousal from sleep, without altering overall sleep structure.

papers.title: DTI-ALPS as a marker of glymphatic function: Review of the literature findings, methodology, and interpretation.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the literature on DTI-ALPS as a marker of glymphatic function, noting exponential growth in publications and its use in various conditions. It concludes that DTI-ALPS is a sensitive but non-specific marker of white matter microstructural damage and neuroinflammation, offering translational potential for clinical screening when combined with other biomarkers.

papers.title: Sleep and psychosis: An integrative review of conceptual and neurophysiological associations.
papers.summary: This integrative review summarizes conceptual and neurophysiological associations between sleep processes (including dreaming and hypnagogia) and psychosis, noting that anterior cingulate and frontal regions may be involved, but direct neurobiological evidence linking sleep to psychosis is limited.

papers.title: A Novel Adversarial Approach for EEG Dataset Refinement: Enhancing Generalization Through Proximity-to-Boundary Scoring.
papers.summary: Proposed a training framework using a proximity-to-boundary score (PBS) to down-weight noisy EEG samples, improving model generalization by 1.43–6.66% on motor imagery and 0.72–2.85% on sleep stage classification datasets without extra hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: Automated autism spectrum disorder detection using EEG signals and time-frequency visibility graphs.
papers.summary: Developed a dual-domain EEG-based ASD detection framework combining time-frequency analysis (STFT, DWT, WVD, SLT) with Horizontal Visibility Graph features; DWT-HVG with a Soft Voting Ensemble achieved 93.54% accuracy and 98.17% AUC, outperforming other methods.

papers.title: An EEG-based fatigue detection framework integrating interpretable feature selection and efficient temporal modeling.
papers.summary: Proposed AXELLSTM, an EEG-based cross-subject fatigue detection framework with interpretable feature selection and EfficientLSTM temporal modeling, achieving 0.7143 Macro-F1 under LOSO validation with low complexity (0.1959M parameters, 3.7069M FLOPs).

papers.title: Acute sleep deprivation rank-dependently enhances offensive aggression via the PVN in male mice.
papers.summary: In male mice, 12-hour acute sleep deprivation selectively increased offensive aggression in dominant (not subordinate) mice, associated with reduced mPFC and increased PVN activation; chemogenetic inhibition of PVN neurons reversed this effect, indicating PVN-dependent mechanisms.

papers.title: Association Between Nocturnal Oxygen Desaturation and the Severity of Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of OSA patients found that AHI was positively correlated with oxygen desaturation index and T90, and inversely correlated with minimum and mean nocturnal SpO2, suggesting related physiological patterns but not establishing causality or clinical utility.

papers.title: Parent and child-reported acceptability and preference of pediatric home sleep apnea testing versus In-lab polysomnography: a pilot study.
papers.summary: In this pilot study of children undergoing PSG and home sleep apnea testing (HSAT), HSAT was feasible and preferred by parents over PSG (60% vs 33% for children), though children frequently required sensor adjustments, suggesting potential for wider acceptance with improved sensor stability.

papers.title: A Multi-Scale Adaptive EEG Feature Selection and Weighting Method for Mental Workload Estimation in Rapid Serial Visual Presentation.
papers.summary: This study developed a Multi-scale Adaptive Feature selection and Augmented Weighting (MAFA) framework for mental workload classification in RSVP-BCIs, achieving higher accuracy than comparison methods and adaptively focusing on posterior theta and alpha band features, demonstrating feasibility and interpretability.

papers.title: Physiologic and symptomatic burden across sleep-disordered breathing severity in men and women.
papers.summary: Analyzing community-based data, this study found that men and women with equivalent SDB severity differ in physiologic and symptomatic burden: men had greater sleep disruption and sleepiness, while women had more insomnia symptoms and lower quality of life, indicating the need to consider sex-specific impacts beyond AHI.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity and Independent Correlates of Cognitive Impairment in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: This study found that patients with atrial fibrillation and cognitive impairment had reduced alpha-band functional connectivity in resting-state EEG, which was independently associated with cognitive impairment and showed good discriminatory ability (AUC 0.814), supporting its potential as a biomarker.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture improves neurocognitive impairment induced by chronic sleep deprivation: an experimental study based on hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity.
papers.summary: In a rat model of chronic sleep deprivation, electroacupuncture at cervical acupoints improved spatial and recognition memory by promoting hippocampal neurogenesis (increasing DCX and Ki-67) and restoring synaptic plasticity in the dentate gyrus, including dendritic spine density and synaptic structure.

papers.title: CEREBROVASCULAR EVENTS AND NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS WITH ALTERATIONS IN POLYSOMNOGRAPHIC INDICATORS FOLLOWING CARDIAC SURGERY.
papers.summary: In a prospective study of 104 cardiac surgery patients, postoperative polysomnographic changes (increased sleep latency and arousal index) correlated with cognitive impairment; citicoline treatment significantly improved cognitive scores and sleep parameter stabilization at 30 days, suggesting PSG as a marker for early neurocognitive dysfunction.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment attenuates chronic stress-induced disruptions in the gut microbiota, intestinal barrier, and brain.
papers.summary: In a chronic unpredictable mild stress mouse model, environmental enrichment reduced depressive-like behavior and reversed stress-induced alterations in gut microbiota composition, intestinal barrier integrity, and brain markers, supporting its role in stabilizing the microbiota-gut-brain axis.

papers.title: From bench to bedside: current evidence and prospects for acupuncture in managing perioperative neurocognitive disorders.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that acupuncture, particularly electroacupuncture and transcutaneous acupoint stimulation, may prevent perioperative neurocognitive disorders by modulating the gut-brain axis, balancing neural circuits, and maintaining synaptic homeostasis, thus reducing risk factors like inflammation and sleep disruption.

papers.title: "Early Stratification of Risk for Poor Neurological Outcome After Cardiac Arrest Is Improved with Processed EEG Data".
papers.summary: Using machine learning on data from 913 comatose cardiac arrest patients, combining early processed EEG metrics (suppression ratio and bispectral index) with clinical data significantly improved prediction of poor neurological outcome at discharge and 6 months (AUC 0.86-0.88), outperforming either dataset alone.
